title: Why Make HTTP Requests from DuckDB?
description: Issue [HTTP](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110) requests directly from a SQL query — no app-layer Python or Node.js between DuckDB and the API. Best fit: ad-hoc REST calls, low-volume per-row enrichment, and one-off integrations. For high-throughput or streaming workloads, keep a real HTTP client.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Three scalar functions — `http_get`, `http_post`, and `http_post_form` — that issue a synchronous HTTP request and return the response as a JSON object you can extract with DuckDB's [JSON operators](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions).

bulletPoints.label: Per-row API enrichment
bulletPoints.description: Join a column against a remote REST endpoint with `http_get` — one HTTP call per row, response parsed inline as JSON. Practical for tens or hundreds of rows; impractical at scale because each call is synchronous.

bulletPoints.label: Ad-hoc API queries
bulletPoints.description: Hit a JSON API from a one-off `SELECT` without writing a script. Combine with [`->>`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions) to pull specific fields out of the response body.

bulletPoints.label: Form-encoded POSTs
bulletPoints.description: `http_post_form` sends parameters as [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1866) — the body shape OAuth token endpoints, older REST APIs, and HTML form handlers expect.

bulletPoints.label: JSON POSTs
bulletPoints.description: `http_post` JSON-encodes the `params` [`MAP`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/map) into the request body. Pair with `headers => MAP{'content-type': 'application/json'}` for REST APIs that consume JSON.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: Each call opens a TCP connection, sends the request, blocks until the response arrives, and returns a JSON struct. There is no `ATTACH`, no secrets type, no connection pool, no retry logic — the extension is intentionally a thin SQL surface over a synchronous HTTP request.

bulletPoints.label: Response shape
bulletPoints.description: Every function returns a JSON object with `status` (the HTTP status code as a number), `reason` (the [HTTP reason phrase](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#name-status-codes) — `"OK"`, `"Not Found"`, etc.), and `body` (the response body as a string). Extract fields with `->>` and cast as needed.

bulletPoints.label: Headers and params are MAPs
bulletPoints.description: Both `http_post` and `http_post_form` take `headers` and `params` as [DuckDB `MAP` literals](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/map) — `MAP{'key': 'value', ...}`. Headers go on the wire as-is; the `params` map is encoded according to which POST function you called.

bulletPoints.label: Synchronous and blocking
bulletPoints.description: DuckDB blocks until the response arrives or the underlying TCP call fails. Slow endpoints stall the query; there is no per-row timeout knob exposed. Use small `LIMIT` clauses or pre-aggregate keys before calling out.

bulletPoints.label: JSON-typed return value
bulletPoints.description: The result is a `JSON` value, so you can chain [`->`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions) and `->>` directly. Cast `(http_get(...)->>'body')::JSON` to dive further into a JSON response body.

sections.title: Scope and caveats
sections.description: The extension is honest-by-design about what it doesn't do. Read this before pointing it at production traffic.

bulletPoints.label: Experimental status
bulletPoints.description: Marked **experimental** by the [upstream README](https://github.com/Query-farm/duckdb-extension-httpclient) — "USE AT YOUR OWN RISK!". Pin a known-good extension version if you depend on it in pipelines.

bulletPoints.label: GET and POST only
bulletPoints.description: No `PUT` / `PATCH` / `DELETE` in the documented surface. For other [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods), shell out to `curl` via [shellfs](/products/extensions/shellfs).

bulletPoints.label: No retries, no backoff, no streaming
bulletPoints.description: The request is issued once and the entire response body is buffered into memory. Build retry / backoff in your application layer, or wrap the call in a CTE that you re-run on failure.

bulletPoints.label: Credentials live in SQL
bulletPoints.description: Bearer tokens and other secrets are passed as plain SQL values in the `headers` map — anything inlined appears in the cached query plan and `EXPLAIN` output. Source from the environment with [`getenv`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/utility#getenv) and bind via [`SET VARIABLE`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/set), as covered in Securing credentials.

bulletPoints.label: One call per row
bulletPoints.description: Per-row enrichment patterns issue one HTTP request per input row. Ten thousand rows means ten thousand sequential calls — slow, and the remote server will likely rate-limit you. Pre-aggregate or cache before joining.

useCases.title: Enrich a small DuckDB result with a REST API
useCases.description: Join a few hundred rows against an external endpoint with `http_get` — geocoding, score lookups, slow-changing reference data. Cache the JSON response into a DuckDB table so repeat queries don't re-hit the API.

useCases.title: Trigger a webhook from a SQL pipeline
useCases.description: End-of-pipeline `http_post` to a webhook URL with a JSON body summarizing what just ran. Synchronous, so the webhook either succeeds or the SQL transaction sees the error.

useCases.title: Exchange OAuth credentials
useCases.description: `http_post_form` against a token endpoint with `grant_type` and credential fields — the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1866) shape OAuth's [Bearer Token spec](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750) requires.

useCases.title: One-off API exploration
useCases.description: Replace `curl` + `jq` with one SQL statement: hit the endpoint, cast the body to JSON, project the fields you want. Keeps the whole investigation inside a single DuckDB session.
